directive: Valerius formally records, personally inducts, equips, and grants personal-guard status to the twenty veterans who proved their worth in Round 87; each retains a distinct fighting style and weapon while training and operating in perfect unison with the rest of the expedition and especially with one another.

events.title: THE NAMES OF THE TWENTY ARE ENTERED BESIDE VALERIUS'S OWN MEN
events.body: At the opening of the new week, Valerius orders the expedition's records amended so that the twenty veterans are no longer listed merely as recent recruits or provisional auxiliaries. Each man's name is entered alongside the names of Valerius's established men, with his veteran service and newly granted guard status recorded. Titus Varenus is entered first among the veterans, followed by Lucius Atilius, Gnaeus Fabius, Marcus Lartius, Publius Servilius, Quintus Vibius, Sextus Tullius, Aulus Decimus, Numerius Cassius, Spurius Calpurnius, Gaius Valerius, Lucius Marcius, Marcus Petronius, Publius Octavius, Quintus Rufrius, Titus Manlius, Gnaeus Licinius, Sextus Cornelius, Aulus Furius, and Lucius Vettienus. The record makes their status explicit: they are now members of Valerius's personal guard, not simply men attached to it for a trial. No enlistment payment is recorded, because their earlier condition remains unchanged.

events.title: VALERIUS PERSONALLY INDUCTS EACH VETERAN
events.body: Valerius personally receives the twenty men one by one rather than treating the appointment as a collective administrative order. Each veteran is called forward by name, receives Valerius's acknowledgement of the service he demonstrated during the proving exercise, and is formally admitted into the guard. The ceremony is deliberately individual because Valerius wants each man to understand that his place was earned through demonstrated conduct rather than granted merely because he arrived with a reputation. The veterans in turn accept the discipline of the guard and swear to act as a single body when Valerius's safety and the column's cohesion require it. The ceremony establishes a personal bond between commander and guard without changing the authority of the expedition's existing officers.

events.title: TWENTY MEN RECEIVE TWENTY DISTINCT SETS OF GEAR
events.body: Valerius orders equipment prepared for each veteran according to the fighting method he demonstrated during the proving exercise rather than issuing an identical kit to all twenty. Titus Varenus receives a short sword and buckler suited to close entry, Lucius Atilius a heavy spear for holding reach, Gnaeus Fabius a long thrusting spear for line control, and the remaining veterans receive combinations of swords, spears, javelins, shields, and one sling according to their demonstrated specialties. The equipment is issued as working field gear rather than ornament, and each man's weapon is entered beside his name in the guard register. The differences give the guard a broad tactical vocabulary without creating separate sub-units that operate independently of Valerius's formation. The men begin drilling immediately with the principle that individual method must remain subordinate to collective movement. Weapon assignments: Titus Varenus: short sword and buckler; Lucius Atilius: heavy spear; Gnaeus Fabius: long thrusting spear; Marcus Lartius: curved sword; Publius Servilius: javelins; Quintus Vibius: spear and oval shield; Sextus Tullius: short sword; Aulus Decimus: light spear; Numerius Cassius: sling; Spurius Calpurnius: heavy spear; Gaius Valerius: sword and shield; Lucius Marcius: javelins and sword; Marcus Petronius: long spear; Publius Octavius: sword and small shield; Quintus Rufrius: spear; Titus Manlius: javelins; Gnaeus Licinius: heavy sword; Sextus Cornelius: spear and shield; Aulus Furius: short sword; Lucius Vettienus: spear.

events.title: INDIVIDUAL FIGHTING STYLES BECOME A SINGLE GUARD SYSTEM
events.body: The first full guard exercise reveals why the veterans' differences do not produce disorder. Each man retains his own preferred method of fighting, but the veterans instinctively regulate distance, timing, and movement around one another. A spear fighter opens space for a swordsman, a javelin man withdraws behind the shield line after throwing, and a close fighter moves into the gap created by the withdrawal without breaking the formation. The same coordination is then practiced with Valerius's established men until the guard can move as part of the expedition's larger loose-phalanx without creating a separate rhythm. Their greatest strength becomes not that twenty men fight alike, but that twenty different methods produce one controlled movement.

events.title: THE GUARD'S OUTER WATCH MOVES AS ONE
events.body: The veterans take their first sustained outer-watch duty as a formally recognized guard. Their individual weapons give them different responses to threats at different distances, yet their spacing remains deliberately synchronized with the rest of Valerius's men. When one veteran shifts position, the neighboring men adjust without verbal confusion, preserving the outward-facing perimeter and the interior movement space established by Valerius's doctrine. Their local-terrain knowledge also allows them to orient their watch around approaches that would otherwise be easy to overlook. The result is a guard that retains twenty distinct fighters while behaving tactically as a single coordinated body.

events.title: THE NEW GUARD PROVES ITS UNITY UNDER PRESSURE
events.body: A sudden field alarm provides the first unscripted test of the newly formalized guard. The twenty veterans react individually according to their specialties, but their movements converge almost immediately into the same defensive pattern practiced during training. No man abandons his assigned role to pursue personal initiative, and the surrounding expeditionary line is not forced to compensate for them. The alarm passes without becoming a battle, but the response gives Valerius a clear demonstration that the veterans' individual fighting styles can coexist with disciplined collective action. The veterans return to their positions without celebration or disorder, treating the successful response as the standard expected of the guard.

events.title: THE PERSONAL GUARD IS FULLY INTEGRATED WITH VALERIUS'S MEN
events.body: By the close of the round, the twenty veterans are functioning as permanent members of Valerius's personal guard while remaining fully integrated with the expedition's established men. Their individual weapons and fighting methods are now documented alongside their names, and their positions can be adjusted without breaking the overall formation. Valerius's direct induction is remembered as the point at which their provisional service became a permanent obligation of guard duty. The veterans have not replaced the expedition's existing soldiers; instead, they add a concentrated layer of experienced local knowledge and highly differentiated combat skills to the same disciplined system. The guard closes the week capable of acting as twenty distinct fighters and, when required, as one coordinated instrument.
